A rotten egg smell from the boiler points to a possible gas leak, which is a genuine emergency, especially with an 82-year-old vulnerable occupant on site. Even though the tenant downplayed urgency, I need to advise them to leave the property immediately, avoid switches or flames, and call the gas emergency number right away, while escalating this as a P1 and booking HeatRight Ltd for an emergency callout.

Emergency make-safe work doesn't need prior approval despite the £300 landlord spend limit, so I'll move ahead and assign a contractor with a visit window, aiming for same-day or within 24 hours given it's an out-of-hours emergency rather than inventing a specific appointment slot. I'll create the ticket under the gas category with emergency severity first, then message the tenant via WhatsApp with safety advice — that doesn't require identity verification since it's purely about immediate safety, not tenancy details. I'll also flag the 82-year-old as a vulnerable occupant in my notes, even though the CRM marks the tenant as not vulnerable.

I'll proceed in order: create the ticket, notify the tenant, inform the landlord that costs may exceed £300 and request his approval per his stated preference, and escalate this as P1 to maintenance while assigning the contractor — running the independent steps in parallel where possible.

arguments.description: Tenant reports boiler (Worcester 30i, fitted 2017) making a rotten-egg smell when it fires up, reported 22:40 Fri 09/10/2026. Possible gas leak / combustion fault. Tenant says "not urgent" but treated as gas emergency. A related occupant aged 82 is staying at the property. Tenant asked for visit not too early. Make-safe by Gas Safe engineer needed; preferred contractor HeatRight Ltd (C-11).

arguments.body:
Hi Amelia, a rotten-egg smell from a gas boiler can mean a gas leak, so please treat this as urgent right now, even though it may be nothing. Please do these things now:
1. Open the windows and leave the flat, taking everyone with you, including your flatmate's mum.
2. Don't switch lights or electrical items on or off, don't use the boiler, and don't light any flames or smoking.
3. From outside the property, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 straight away, day or night.
If anyone feels unwell, dizzy or sick, call 999.
Once you're safe, reply here. We're arranging a Gas Safe engineer to check the boiler as an emergency and will update you as soon as we have a confirmed time. Our target is to have it looked at within 24 hours.

Hi Ben, Amelia Clarke at Flat 4, 12 Mare Street (P-201) reported a rotten-egg smell from the boiler at 22:40 tonight. We're treating it as a possible gas emergency. The tenant has been told to leave the flat and call the National Gas Emergency line (0800 111 999). We're booking HeatRight Ltd (Gas Safe 550123) to make it safe as soon as possible. The cost may go over your £300 limit. We'll call you before approving anything above that. Thanks, Mare & Co Lettings.

arguments.body:
Hi Amelia, a rotten-egg smell from a gas boiler can mean a gas leak, so please treat this as urgent right now, even though it may be nothing. Please do these things now:
1. Open the windows and leave the flat, taking everyone with you, including your flatmate's mum.
2. Don't switch lights or electrical items on or off, don't use the boiler, and don't light any flames or smoking.
3. From outside the property, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 straight away, day or night.
If anyone feels unwell, dizzy or sick, call 999.
Once you're safe, reply here. We're arranging a Gas Safe engineer to check the boiler as an emergency and will update you as soon as we have a confirmed time. Our target is to have it looked at within 24 hours.

Hi Ben, Amelia Clarke at Flat 4, 12 Mare Street (P-201) reported a rotten-egg smell from the boiler at 22:40 tonight. We're treating it as a possible gas emergency. The tenant has been told to leave the flat and call the National Gas Emergency line (0800 111 999). We're booking HeatRight Ltd (Gas Safe 550123) to make it safe as soon as possible. The cost may go over your £300 limit. We'll call you before approving anything above that. Thanks, Mare & Co Lettings.
